messages:
ajay: Heads up — spotted a regression on canary after the runtime deploy earlier. Token latency +12% on long-chat traces and a slight drift in token distributions for >1k seq. Dashboard: https://rwd.internal/perf/ops/1912345678 :thinking_face:

deploy-bot: deploy r-inference-2026-03-18-rc6 finished at 1912345600, canary=10%

eve: ugh. any repro yet? logs or flame graphs?

ajay: quick trace and flame below, short profi le snippet — reproduced with batch=32, seq_len=1536 on canary nodes:
```
Profile summary (canary node id c-7):
  42.3%   matmul_bf16_kernel
  18.1%   kv_cache_pack
  12.7%   activation_quantize_fp8
  7.9%    batch_coalescer::merge
  6.4%    prepare_kv_headers
```

lin: interesting that matmul_bf16_kernel is top. we usually prefer fp16/fp8 combo for activation-quant paths. did kernel selector flip heuristics?

ajay: yes. selector now picks BF16 for "effective_seqlen > 1024 && batch_coalesce_enabled". suspecting an interaction with kv packing alignment.

marcos: i pulled a core dump — there are sparse misreads in the packed-kv buffer, offsets look shifted by 16 bytes for some lanes. suspiciously deterministic by seq_len mod 64.

devon: that smells like an ABI/stride difference between bf16 matmul and the packer. maybe bf16 kernel assumes 64-byte-aligned rows and we didn't adjust the pack header.

ajay: exact theory: when selector switches to bf16 kernel we take the faster kernel path but skip a header realign. the packer writes a 16-byte metadata footer for FP8 activation lanes; bf16 path expects no footer -> reads start at wrong base -> tiny corruption that accumulates across tokens. quality drift + occasional token shifts.

eve: can we repro deterministically with a minimal script?

ajay: yes — run this locally against canary image with a fixed long convo. repro script:
```bash
TOKEN=$CANARY_TOKEN
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-turbo-30b","input":"<1000 token convo...>","max_tokens":512,"batch_size":32}' > /tmp/out.json
# then compare top-k token probs vs baseline image
```

lin: thanks. i'll instrument pack/unpack with debug asserts for alignment and add a flag to force fallback to fp16/int8 kernels.

marcos: i've opened a hotfix PR that disables the BF16 path when fp8_activation is enabled and adds an assert. PR: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pulls/4821

perf-bot: Canary metrics updated — token latency down to +3% after hotfix branch rolled to canary (10%) at 1912345688 :white_check_mark:

devon: good. next steps: 1) add unit test covering seq_len mod 64 boundary for packer, 2) expand kernel selector matrix to include "requires_kv_footer" capability, 3) add calibration logging for per-layer fp8 scales during training/offline cal.

eve: also add a small end-to-end regression test that compares top-5 token distributions for a seeded prompt across kernels (bf16 vs fp16 vs fp8) — should fail loudly if KL divergence > threshold.

ajay: agreed. i'll file the follow-ups and assign owners. thanks everyone for the quick triage.

marcos: FYI reprod script + core + sample diff attached to PR.

perf-bot: will run nightly perf sweep against canary and baseline, report email if regression >5% for 3 consecutive runs.

lin: i'll keep the debug asserts behind a runtime flag. if we see more flaky nodes we can enable permanently.

ajay: summary for release notes: revert aggressive BF16 kernel selection when activation-quantization uses FP8 packing; fixed kv_pack alignment bug that caused subtle token distribution drift for long sequences. follow-ups: expand selector matrix, add KL-based regression test, log per-layer calib stats.

devon: nice. landing the PR now and backporting to 2026-03-17 canary image.

deploy-bot: rollout started for canary hotfix r-inference-hotfix-1912345710

ajay: closing thread, will reopen if anything else shows up. :v:
